cover.body_html:
30亿欧元。

这不是某个美国AI独角兽又一轮夸张的融资，而是一家成立不到三年的法国公司，在周二宣布拿到的D轮。9月8日，Mistral AI正式对外确认完成30亿欧元（约35亿美元）的D轮融资，投后估值超过210亿欧元（约245亿美元）。三星电子领投，EQT旗下Scaleup Europe Fund和现有投资者PSG Equity联合领投。

这笔融资有三个纪录：欧洲科技史上最大单笔股权融资、开源大模型阵营估值最高的公司之一、今年全球范围内金额最大的AI公司融资。更重要的是，它不是发生在旧金山、不是在西雅图、不是在北京——它发生在巴黎。

为什么是三星，为什么是Mistral

三星领投这件事，比30亿欧元这个数字更值得琢磨。

过去几年，全球AI算力和模型的话语权高度集中在英伟达和少数美国公司手里。OpenAI绑定微软、Anthropic绑定Google、xAI绑定马斯克和自己的数据中心——每一家前沿大模型公司背后，都站着一个算力巨头。这种「软件+硬件」的深度绑定，让后来者很难有机会。

但三星是个例外。这家韩国巨头手里有全球最先进的存储芯片和HBM产能，有自己的Exynos处理器，有手机、电视、家电等海量终端场景，唯独缺一个能打的AI基础模型。它之前也投过AI公司，但更多是财务投资。这次不一样。

Mistral对三星的价值，是补全了三星AI战略的最后一块拼图：从芯片到设备到模型的全链路。想想看——三星的手机、电视、家电、可穿戴设备，全球出货量超过10亿台，这些设备都需要端侧AI能力。Mistral的小模型路线（7B、8x7B MoE）天然适合端侧部署，两者的契合度极高。

而三星对Mistral的价值，则是实实在在的硬件支持和场景落地。有了三星这个战略投资人，Mistral在端侧模型的优化上可以直接拿到最底层的硬件信息，在手机、电视等场景的落地可以走得比其他模型快几个身位。这不是一笔单纯的财务投资，这是一次深度的战略结盟。

"闭源模型越走越贵、越走越封闭的时候，开源阵营需要一个能站在最前排的选手。Mistral正在成为那个选手。"—— 一位AI行业投资人的判断

开源AI的第二极，终于站到了台前

Mistral的崛起，有一个更大的背景：开源大模型阵营正在重新洗牌。

过去两年，开源模型的叙事基本由Meta的Llama系列主导。Llama 2、Llama 3，每一代发布都会带动一波开源创新浪潮。但Llama有一个根本性的问题：它不是真正的开源。商用需要授权、有使用门槛、有各种限制条件，与其说是开源，不如说是「开放权重」。

Mistral走的是另一条路。从Mistral 7B到Mixtral 8x7B，再到后来的Mistral Large和Mistral Small，这家法国公司在开源社区的声望一路走高。它的模型不仅性能强劲，而且对开发者极其友好——权重开放、API便宜、文档清晰、社区活跃。

更关键的是，Mistral证明了一件事：开源模型不仅能在实验室里跑分，还能在商业上赚钱。据业界估算，Mistral的年化收入已经达到数亿欧元级别，客户遍布欧洲和北美。这在开源模型公司里是罕见的——大多数开源模型团队要么靠融资烧钱、要么靠云厂商采购，自身造血能力很弱。

210亿欧元的估值是什么概念？作为对比，去年同期大家热议的Anthropic估值约为600亿美元，OpenAI估值超过1500亿美元。Mistral的估值虽然只有它们的几分之一，但考虑到Mistral走的是开源路线、团队规模小得多、成立时间短得多，这个数字已经相当惊人。

更重要的是位置。在全球AI大模型的版图上，美国有OpenAI、Anthropic、Google、Meta，中国有智谱、月之暗面、DeepSeek、通义千问。欧洲一直是个空白——有研究、有人才、有市场，但缺少一家能打的本土大模型公司。Mistral正在填补这个空白。

三个层面的连锁反应

这笔融资的影响，会在三个层面展开。

第一个层面是市场竞争。有了30亿欧元的弹药，Mistral会在算力投入、模型研发、商业化拓展三个方向同时加速。之前很多人觉得开源模型追不上闭源第一梯队——性能差距确实存在，但Mistral正在用实际行动缩小这个差距。有了充足的算力和人才储备，下一代Mistral模型可能会在更多基准测试上逼近甚至超过闭源模型。这对整个行业都是好事——竞争越激烈，进步就越快，价格就越低。

第二个层面是地缘政治。美国AI出口管制越收越紧，欧洲和亚洲的企业都在寻找「不依赖美国」的替代方案。Mistral作为一家欧洲公司，天然不受美国出口管制的直接约束，这对很多企业来说是巨大的吸引力。三星的投资更是强化了这个定位——一个欧洲模型公司，加一个亚洲硬件巨头，等于一条绕开美国的AI供应链。

第三个层面是开源生态。过去开源模型的最大痛点是「没人愿意持续投入重金研发」——开源不赚钱是行业共识。但Mistral用210亿的估值告诉市场：开源也能长出大公司，也能获得高估值。这会吸引更多资本进入开源AI领域，形成正循环。资本进来了，人才就来了；人才来了，模型就进步了；模型进步了，商业价值就兑现了。

不是终局，是开局

当然，210亿欧元估值的Mistral也面临巨大的挑战。

最大的挑战是算力。前沿大模型的训练越来越烧钱，30亿欧元听起来很多，但在大模型训练面前，可能也就够训练一两个旗舰模型的。OpenAI一年的算力投入是百亿美元级别的，Mistral要追这个差距，30亿只是起步。

第二个挑战是商业化。开源模型的商业化一直是个难题。Mistral目前的收入主要来自API服务和企业定制，这两块的竞争都非常激烈——上面有OpenAI、Anthropic的闭源模型压着，下面有无数开源小模型在卷价格。如何在保持开源初心的同时实现大规模商业化，是Mistral必须回答的问题。

第三个挑战是人才。欧洲的AI人才储备虽然不错，但和美国比还是有差距。Mistral要扩张团队，必须从全球招募顶尖人才，这意味着更高的薪酬、更激烈的人才争夺。

但无论如何，Mistral的这一轮融资都是一个标志性事件。它标志着几件事：

第一，开源AI终于有了一个能站在舞台中央的玩家。之前开源模型虽然热闹，但更多是社区驱动、小团队玩票。现在有了三星背书、210亿估值的Mistral，开源阵营在和闭源巨头对话时，腰板可以更硬了。

第二，AI的地缘格局正在从「美国独大」走向「多极化」。美国有OpenAI/Google/Anthropic，中国有智谱/DeepSeek/通义，欧洲有Mistral——三足鼎立的雏形已经显现。这对整个行业的健康发展是好事，没有任何一个地区应该垄断AI的未来。

第三，硬件和软件的结盟正在成为新常态。三星+Mistral、英伟达+一众云厂商、微软+OpenAI、Google+Anthropic——每一个前沿AI玩家背后，都站着一个甚至多个硬件巨头。AI竞争已经不是模型之间的竞争，而是生态系统之间的竞争。

30亿欧元不是终局，是Mistral下一轮冲刺的开局。AI产业的故事，远比我们想象的更漫长、更精彩。

明天见。
cover.body_html_en:
Three billion euros.

This isn't another overhyped funding round from a San Francisco AI unicorn. It's a Series D announced on Tuesday by a French company founded less than three years ago. On September 8, Mistral AI officially confirmed closing a €3 billion (~$3.5 billion) Series D at a post-money valuation of over €21 billion (~$24.5 billion). Samsung Electronics led the round, with EQT's Scaleup Europe Fund and existing investor PSG Equity co-leading.

This round sets three records: Europe's largest single equity round in tech history, one of the highest valuations in the open-source LLM camp, and the largest AI company funding round globally this year. Most importantly — it didn't happen in San Francisco, or Seattle, or Beijing. It happened in Paris.

Why Samsung, Why Mistral

Samsung leading the round is more telling than the €3 billion figure itself.

Over the past few years, global AI compute and model power have been heavily concentrated in Nvidia and a handful of American companies. OpenAI is tied to Microsoft, Anthropic to Google, xAI to Musk and its own data centers — behind every frontier LLM company stands a compute giant. This deep "software + hardware" coupling has made it extremely hard for newcomers to break in.

But Samsung is the exception. The Korean giant has the world's most advanced memory chips and HBM capacity, its own Exynos processors, and massive end-device scenarios across phones, TVs, and home appliances. What it's missing is a competitive AI foundation model. It has invested in AI companies before, but mostly financially — this time is different.

Mistral's value to Samsung is completing the last piece of Samsung's AI strategy puzzle: an end-to-end chain from chip to device to model. Think about it — Samsung ships over a billion devices globally: phones, TVs, appliances, wearables. All of them need on-device AI capabilities. Mistral's small-model approach (7B, 8x7B MoE) is naturally suited for edge deployment. The fit is almost perfect.

And Samsung's value to Mistral is tangible hardware support and scenario deployment. With Samsung as a strategic investor, Mistral can get the lowest-level hardware information directly for edge model optimization, and can move faster than any other model in deploying to phones, TVs, and more. This isn't purely financial — it's a deep strategic alliance.

"As closed-source models grow more expensive and more locked down by the day, the open-source camp needs a player that can stand on the front row. Mistral is becoming that player."— An AI industry investor's assessment

Open-Source AI's Second Pole Finally Steps Into the Spotlight

Mistral's rise fits into a bigger picture: the open-source LLM landscape is reshuffling.

For the past two years, the open-source narrative has been dominated by Meta's Llama series. Llama 2, Llama 3 — each release has driven a wave of open-source innovation. But Llama has a fundamental problem: it's not truly open source. Commercial use requires licensing, there are usage thresholds, all kinds of restrictions. It's less "open source" and more "open weights."

Mistral is taking a different path. From Mistral 7B to Mixtral 8x7B, to Mistral Large and Mistral Small, the French company's reputation in the open-source community has skyrocketed. Its models don't just perform well — they're extremely developer-friendly: open weights, cheap APIs, clear documentation, an active community.

More critically, Mistral has proven something: open-source models don't just score well in benchmarks — they can make money. Industry estimates put Mistral's annualized revenue at several hundred million euros, with customers across Europe and North America. That's rare among open-source model companies — most either burn through funding or rely on cloud vendor purchases, with weak self-sustaining revenue.

What does a €21 billion valuation mean? For context, Anthropic was valued at roughly $60 billion around this time last year, and OpenAI at over $150 billion. Mistral's valuation is only a fraction of theirs — but considering Mistral's open-source route, much smaller team, and much shorter history, the number is already staggering.

What matters more is position. On the global LLM map, the U.S. has OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta. China has Zhipu, Moonshot, DeepSeek, Qwen. Europe has been a blank spot — research, talent, and market exist, but there's been no competitive homegrown LLM company. Mistral is filling that gap.

Three Layers of Ripple Effects

The impact of this round will unfold on three levels.

Level one: market competition. With €3 billion in ammunition, Mistral will accelerate on three fronts simultaneously — compute investment, model R&D, and commercial expansion. Many people used to think open-source models could never catch up to closed-source first-tier players — the performance gap is real, but Mistral is narrowing it with actual execution. With sufficient compute and talent, the next generation of Mistral models could approach or even surpass closed-source models on more benchmarks. That's good for the entire industry — more competition means faster progress and lower prices.

Level two: geopolitics. As U.S. AI export controls tighten further and further, companies in Europe and Asia are looking for alternatives that "don't depend on the U.S." As a European company, Mistral is naturally not directly subject to U.S. export controls — a huge draw for many enterprises. Samsung's investment reinforces this positioning: a European model company plus an Asian hardware giant equals an AI supply chain that bypasses the U.S.

Level three: the open-source ecosystem. Historically, the biggest pain point for open-source models has been "nobody wants to pour serious money into R&D" — the consensus has been that open source doesn't make money. But Mistral, with its €21 billion valuation, is telling the market: open source can also grow big companies and command high valuations. This will attract more capital into open-source AI, creating a positive flywheel. Capital comes in, talent follows; talent arrives, models improve; models get better, commercial value materializes.

Not the Endgame — the Opening

Of course, Mistral at €21 billion also faces enormous challenges.

The biggest challenge is compute. Training frontier LLMs is getting more and more expensive. €3 billion sounds like a lot, but in the face of large model training costs, it might only be enough to train one or two flagship models. OpenAI's annual compute spend is in the tens of billions of dollars. For Mistral to close that gap, €3 billion is just the starting line.

The second challenge is commercialization. Monetizing open-source models has always been hard. Mistral's current revenue comes mainly from API services and enterprise customization — both fiercely competitive markets. Above them are the closed-source incumbents like OpenAI and Anthropic; below them, countless open-source small models are racing prices to the bottom. How to achieve large-scale commercialization while staying true to its open-source roots is the question Mistral must answer.

The third challenge is talent. Europe has decent AI talent reserves, but still lags behind the U.S. To expand its team, Mistral will have to recruit top talent globally — meaning higher compensation and fiercer talent competition.

Regardless, this round is a landmark event. It signals three things:

First, open-source AI finally has a player that can stand center stage. Previously, although open-source models had buzz, it was mostly community-driven, small-team side projects. Now, with Samsung's backing and a €21 billion valuation, the open-source camp can stand a little taller when negotiating with closed-source giants.

Second, AI's geopolitical landscape is shifting from "U.S. dominance" to "multipolarity". The U.S. has OpenAI/Google/Anthropic, China has Zhipu/DeepSeek/Qwen, Europe has Mistral — the outline of a three-pole world is already visible. That's healthy for the industry's long-term development. No single region should monopolize AI's future.

Third, hardware-software alliances are becoming the new normal. Samsung+Mistral, Nvidia+cloud vendors, Microsoft+OpenAI, Google+Anthropic — behind every frontier AI player stands one or more hardware giants. AI competition is no longer between models — it's between ecosystems.

€3 billion isn't the endgame. It's the starting line for Mistral's next sprint. The story of the AI industry is far longer and more fascinating than any of us imagined.

See you tomorrow.

briefs.body_html:
用Cursor或Copilot写代码的人，大概都经历过这种崩溃：浏览器标签页一关、IDE一退，刚才那个陪你写了一下午的Agent就没了。明天打开，又是一个崭新的、啥也不记得的AI。

你才是那个集成层。你一离开，流程就停。

9月7日，亚马逊云科技开源的Kiro Crew，恰恰瞄准了这个痛点。这套多Agent协同系统的核心只有一个诉求：让编码任务可以跨会话持续运行，你丢完任务就走，回来收结果。它源自Amazon内部的MeshClaw项目，已经在内部服务了超过3.9万名开发者。

从Vibe Coding到异步托管，差在哪

目前大多数AI编程工具还停留在「Vibe Coding」阶段——你坐在屏幕前，跟Agent一句一句聊，它写一段你review一段，整个人被钉在工位上。效率确实提高了，但你的时间还是被绑定着。

Kiro Crew做的事，是把编程Agent从「聊天窗口里的助手」变成「后台跑着的worker」。它支持跨会话状态保持，意思是：你下午五点给它丢一个重构任务，关电脑下班，第二天早上打开就能看到结果。中间它自己规划步骤、自己调用工具、自己遇到错误重试、自己推进进度。

支撑这件事的，是三个关键设计：

第一，共享记忆与可复用Skills。多个Agent可以共享同一份项目上下文和知识库，不需要每次都重新喂代码库。Skill可以被封装复用，就像函数调用一样。

第二，多Agent并行调度。一个大任务可以拆成多个子任务，同时派出好几个Agent分头去做——有的写测试、有的改文档、有的做重构。最后汇总结果。

第三，定时触发与Webhook集成。Agent可以在特定时间自动运行（比如每天凌晨做一次代码巡检），也可以通过MCP和Webhook对接外部系统——CI挂了自动排查、issue新建了自动分配。

3.9万内部用户验证的工程化路径

Kiro Crew不是实验室里的Demo，而是在Amazon内部跑了一段时间的生产级工具。

3.9万内部开发者是什么概念？这意味着它经历过真实大规模场景的拷打——代码库的规模、任务的多样性、出错的各种奇葩情况，都不是小团队实验能模拟的。亚马逊杰出开发者布道师Darko Mesaroš在分享中说过一句话：长期运行并不意味着让模型无限循环，而是让任务能够跨越多个会话持续推进，同时保留必要的上下文、执行记录和人工干预入口。

这里面最值得注意的一点是「人工干预入口」。很多人一听到「异步Agent」就担心失控——Agent跑飞了怎么办？把代码删了怎么办？Kiro Crew的答案是细粒度的安全控制和可观测性：每一步操作都有记录、关键节点需要人确认、出了问题随时可以介入。

这才是工程化的AI编程工具该有的样子。不是酷炫的Demo，而是可管、可控、可审计、能在真实团队里落地的生产力工具。

AI编程的第一幕是Vibe Coding——你坐在屏幕前，和Agent一起写代码，效率提升了，但人还是那个瓶颈。第二幕正在拉开：异步托管的Agent在后台跑，人从「监工」变成「决策者」，真正从重复性工作里解放出来。

Kiro Crew开源只是一个起点。当越来越多的Agent从聊天框里走出来、走进后台持续运行，软件开发的协作方式会被重新定义。

明天见。
briefs.body_html_en:
Anyone who's used Cursor or Copilot to write code has probably had this moment of frustration: close the browser tab, quit the IDE, and that agent you spent all afternoon pairing with is just gone. Open it up tomorrow, and you've got a brand-new AI that remembers nothing.

You're the integration layer. The moment you leave, the process stops.

On September 7, Amazon Web Services open-sourced Kiro Crew — a multi-agent collaborative system built to fix exactly this pain point. Its core mission is simple: let coding tasks run persistently across sessions. Drop the task, walk away, come back to results. Born from Amazon's internal MeshClaw project, it already serves over 39,000 developers internally.

From Vibe Coding to Async Hosting — What's the Difference?

Most AI coding tools today are still stuck in the "vibe coding" phase: you sit in front of the screen, chat with the agent line by line, it writes a bit, you review a bit. Your productivity goes up, but your time is still tied to the process.

What Kiro Crew does is turn coding agents from "chat window assistants" into "background workers." It supports cross-session state preservation — meaning you can drop a refactoring task at 5pm, shut down your computer, and see results the next morning. In between, it plans its own steps, calls its own tools, retries on its own when things fail, and keeps making progress.

Three key design choices make this work:

First, shared memory and reusable Skills. Multiple agents can share the same project context and knowledge base — no need to re-feed the codebase every time. Skills can be encapsulated and reused, just like function calls.

Second, multi-agent parallel scheduling. A big task can be split into subtasks, dispatched to several agents working simultaneously — one writing tests, one updating docs, one doing refactoring. Results get merged at the end.

Third, scheduled triggers and Webhook integration. Agents can run automatically at specific times (like a nightly code audit), or connect to external systems via MCP and Webhooks — auto-investigate when CI breaks, auto-triage when a new issue is filed.

The Engineering Path Validated by 39,000 Internal Users

Kiro Crew isn't a lab demo — it's a production-grade tool that's been running inside Amazon for a while.

39,000 internal developers means it's been battle-tested at real scale — the size of the codebases, the diversity of tasks, all the weird ways things can go wrong — none of that can be simulated by a small team experiment. Darko Mesaroš, AWS Principal Developer Advocate, put it this way: long-running doesn't mean letting the model loop forever. It means tasks can progress across multiple sessions while preserving necessary context, execution logs, and human intervention points.

The most important detail here is "human intervention points." A lot of people hear "async agent" and panic about loss of control — what if the agent runs amok? What if it deletes code? Kiro Crew's answer is fine-grained security control and observability: every operation is logged, critical junctures require human approval, and you can step in anytime something goes wrong.

That's what engineering-grade AI coding tools look like. Not flashy demos — but manageable, controllable, auditable productivity tools that actually land in real teams.

The first act of AI coding was vibe coding — you sit at the screen, pair with an agent, efficiency improves, but you're still the bottleneck. The second act is starting now: async hosted agents running in the background, humans moving from supervisors to decision-makers, finally being freed from repetitive work.

Kiro Crew going open source is just the starting point. As more agents step out of chat boxes and into persistent background execution, the way software development gets done will be redefined.

See you tomorrow.

briefs.body_html:
说到Agent，你脑海里的画面大概是这样的：云端几百亿参数的大模型，跑着几百美元一天的算力，调用十几个工具，帮你完成复杂任务。端侧模型？那是用来做翻译、摘要、语音识别这种轻活儿的。

但面壁智能9月8日开源的MiniCPM5-2B，正在推翻这个刻板印象。

这款只有25.2亿参数的稠密模型，在Agentic Index上拿到了20分。听起来不高？但同等参数规模的其他模型，得分普遍还在10分以下。换句话说，在2B这个量级上，MiniCPM5把端侧Agent的能力基线往上提了一倍。

Agentic Index 20分意味着什么

Agentic Index是衡量模型工具调用、深度搜索、代码生成等智能体核心能力的综合指标。分数越高，说明模型越能独立完成复杂任务——不是简单回答问题，而是能调用工具、规划步骤、处理错误、迭代推进。

20分放在云端大模型里可能不算什么，但在端侧场景下意义完全不同。它意味着一个完全跑在你手机、PC、车机本地的模型，可以完成：

· 基本的工具调用和函数执行
· 多步骤任务规划
· 代码生成与简单调试
· 本地文档搜索与摘要

这些能力如果放在一年前，你必须调用云端API才能实现。现在它们可以在你的设备上跑，数据不用出本地，推理不需要花钱，延迟几乎为零。

更重要的是基础架构。MiniCPM5-2B采用标准LlamaForCausalLM架构，支持vLLM、SGLang、llama.cpp、Ollama等主流推理引擎——这意味着开发者不用折腾新工具链，拿来就能用。原生131,072 token的上下文长度，在端侧模型里也是第一梯队的水平。

端侧Agent的两个核心驱动力

为什么端侧Agent这件事这么重要？因为它同时解决了两个企业最头疼的问题。

第一个是数据安全。企业用云端Agent最大的顾虑是什么？代码、文档、客户数据全要传给第三方模型，数据泄露的风险如影随形。如果Agent能在企业内网、甚至在员工的PC本地跑，数据不出公司大门——这个顾虑就没了。金融、医疗、政府这些对数据敏感的行业，端侧Agent几乎是刚需。

第二个是推理成本。大模型API按token计费，用得越多花得越多。一个重度Agent用户一天可能消耗几百万甚至上千万token，成本相当可观。如果常用的80%任务可以由端侧小模型搞定，只把最复杂的20%交给云端——总体推理成本可能下降一个数量级。

MiniCPM系列不是第一次刷新端侧模型的认知了。截至2026年6月，MiniCPM开源系列累计下载量已经突破3800万次，GitHub上超过14万颗星。这说明端侧模型的需求是真实存在的，而且在快速增长。

当然，20分还远不是终点。云端前沿模型的Agent能力在持续进化，端侧要追的路还很长。但关键的一步已经迈出去了：端侧模型从「能回答问题」进化到了「能做任务」。

未来的AI架构很可能是混合的——简单任务端侧搞定、复杂任务云端处理、两者无缝切换。到那一天，Agent才算真正走进了每个人的设备。

明天见。
briefs.body_html_en:
When you hear "agent," you probably picture this: a cloud-based model with tens of billions of parameters, burning hundreds of dollars a day in compute, calling dozens of tools to help you complete complex tasks. Edge models? Those are for light work — translation, summarization, speech recognition.

But MiniCPM5-2B, open-sourced by MiniCPM (Facewall Intelligence) on September 8, is upending that stereotype.

This dense model with only 2.52 billion parameters scored 20 on the Agentic Index. Doesn't sound high? But other models at the same parameter scale are generally stuck below 10. In other words, at the 2B level, MiniCPM5 has doubled the baseline for edge agent capability.

What Does an Agentic Index of 20 Actually Mean?

Agentic Index is a composite metric measuring core agent capabilities: tool use, deep search, code generation, and more. A higher score means the model can independently complete complex tasks — not just answer questions, but call tools, plan steps, handle errors, and iterate forward.

Twenty points might not impress anyone looking at cloud frontier models, but in edge scenarios the meaning is completely different. It means a model running entirely on your phone, PC, or car can do:

· Basic tool calling and function execution
· Multi-step task planning
· Code generation and simple debugging
· Local document search and summarization

If you go back a year, these capabilities all required calling a cloud API. Now they can run on your device — data never leaves the device, inference costs nothing, and latency is near zero.

What matters even more is the architecture. MiniCPM5-2B uses the standard LlamaForCausalLM architecture and supports all major inference engines: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama — meaning developers don't have to learn a new toolchain. It just works. And a native context length of 131,072 tokens puts it in the top tier among edge models.

Two Core Drivers for Edge Agents

Why does edge agent stuff matter so much? Because it solves two of enterprise's biggest headaches at once.

First is data security. What's the biggest concern for enterprises using cloud agents? Code, documents, customer data — all getting sent to third-party models, with data breach risk looming over everything. If agents can run on the corporate intranet, or even locally on an employee's PC, with data never leaving the building — that concern vanishes. For data-sensitive industries like finance, healthcare, and government, edge agents are almost a necessity.

Second is inference cost. LLM APIs charge by the token — the more you use, the more you spend. A heavy agent user can consume millions or even tens of millions of tokens a day, which adds up fast. If 80% of common tasks can be handled by small edge models, and only the hardest 20% go to the cloud — overall inference costs could drop by an order of magnitude.

This isn't the first time the MiniCPM series has redefined expectations for edge models. As of June 2026, the MiniCPM open-source series had surpassed 38 million cumulative downloads, with over 140,000 GitHub stars. That tells you the demand for edge models is real — and growing fast.

Of course, 20 points is far from the finish line. Cloud frontier models keep evolving their agent capabilities, and the edge has a long way to go to catch up. But the critical step has been taken: edge models have evolved from "answering questions" to "getting things done."

Future AI architectures will likely be hybrid — simple tasks handled on-device, complex tasks sent to the cloud, switching seamlessly between the two. When that day comes, agents will have truly arrived on everyone's devices.

See you tomorrow.

briefs.body_html:
「一人公司」这四个字，第一次出现在了国家级政策文件里。

工信部印发的《人工智能中小企业创业支持计划（2026—2028年）》里有这么一句话：鼓励各地对依托智能工具开展敏捷创业的「一人公司」、超级个体等微型主体给予包容支持。

看起来只是一句普通表述，但它的分量不轻。在此之前，「一人公司」更多是创业者圈子里的说法——一个人加一套AI工具，从零开始做产品、做内容、做服务，营收可能不小，但公司只有一个人。官方层面从来没有给过一个明确的名分。

现在有了。

政策终于追上了现实

一人公司不是什么新概念。但AI让这件事的量级和爆发力完全不同了。

以前你一个人创业，能做的事情很有限——开发做不了设计、做内容做不了运营、做销售做不了客服。每缺一个职能，你要么自己硬扛（效率低），要么雇人（成本高），要么外包（质量没保障）。一个人能做的业务天花板很低。

AI把这个天花板捅破了。一个开发者可以用AI做设计、做文案、做客服、做数据分析；一个内容创作者可以用AI做剪辑、做封面、做选题、做分发。原本需要三五个人的团队，现在一个人加上一组AI工具就能搞定。

这件事已经在真实发生了。武汉江岸区的「众生云OPC生态社区」，入驻的一人公司创业者靠AI工具做短视频，单条作品平均浏览量突破4万。Indie Hackers上，一个人的SaaS产品月入过万美元的案例越来越多。不是个别现象，是越来越普遍的趋势。

工信部这份文件的意义，不是给了多少钱（虽然普惠算力也是真金白银），而是给了一种确定性：一人公司是被认可的、是被支持的、是有政策配套的。对很多想创业又犹豫的人来说，这份确定性比补贴更重要。

四个方面，最值得关注的是什么

整份计划有4方面15项重点任务，普通创业者最值得关注的有三点。

第一是普惠算力。深入实施普惠算力赋能中小企业发展专项行动——这意味着初创团队和个人开发者，未来可能以更低的成本甚至免费拿到算力资源。算力是AI创业最大的固定成本之一，如果这块能降下来，创业门槛会再低一截。

第二是智能原生企业培育。加快培育「智能原生」企业——从诞生第一天起就深度依赖AI的公司，而不是传统企业再加一层AI。这意味着政策资源会向真正的AI原生创业项目倾斜，而不是撒胡椒面。

第三是配套政策探索。探索根据企业自主评价结果落实落户安居、医疗保障等配套政策。这句话的潜台词是：未来一个人开公司，也可能享受到和大公司员工一样的公共服务保障。这对创业者来说是最实在的安全感。

当然，政策只是外部条件。创业能不能成，最终还是靠产品、靠市场、靠执行力。但不可否认的是：当AI把创业的边际成本压到趋近于零，当政策给了一人公司明确的名分，想试试的人会越来越多。

未来三年，我们可能会看到一波前所未有的AI创业潮——不是那种拿融资烧钱的创业，而是一个人、一台电脑、一组AI工具，从一个小切口开始慢慢长大的创业。它们可能永远不会成为独角兽，但它们会是经济生态里最有活力的那部分。

明天见。
briefs.body_html_en:
The term "one-person company" has appeared in a national policy document for the first time.

Buried in MIIT's "AI SME Startup Support Plan (2026–2028)" is this line: Encourage local governments to give inclusive support to "one-person companies," super individuals, and other micro-entities that rely on intelligent tools for agile entrepreneurship.

It might look like an ordinary sentence, but its weight shouldn't be underestimated. Until now, "one-person company" was mostly a phrase used in founder circles — one person plus a set of AI tools, building products, creating content, delivering services from scratch, maybe generating significant revenue while employing just one person. There was never an official designation for it at the national level.

Now there is.

Policy Has Finally Caught Up to Reality

One-person companies aren't a new concept. But AI has completely changed the scale and explosive potential of this model.

Before, when you started a business alone, what you could do was very limited. A developer couldn't do design, a content creator couldn't do operations, a salesperson couldn't do customer support. For every missing function, you either struggled through it yourself (low efficiency), hired someone (high cost), or outsourced it (unreliable quality). The revenue ceiling for a solo operation was very low.

AI has smashed through that ceiling. A developer can use AI for design, copywriting, customer support, data analysis. A content creator can use AI for editing, thumbnails, topic selection, distribution. What used to take a team of three to five people can now be handled by one person with a stack of AI tools.

This is already happening for real. In Wuhan's Jiang'an district, "ZhongSheng Cloud OPC Ecological Community" hosts one-person company founders who use AI tools to make short videos, with average views per piece exceeding 40,000. On Indie Hackers, there are more and more cases of single-person SaaS products hitting five-figure monthly revenue. It's not an anomaly — it's a growing trend.

The significance of this MIIT document isn't about how much money it allocates (though inclusive compute is real money). It's about giving certainty: one-person companies are recognized, supported, and have policy backing. For many people hesitating to start something, that certainty matters more than subsidies.

Four Areas — What Matters Most for Regular Founders

The plan covers four areas with 15 key tasks. For ordinary founders, three points matter most.

First: inclusive compute. Deeply implementing the inclusive compute empowerment action for SMEs — this means early-stage teams and solo developers might get access to compute resources at lower cost, or even for free. Compute is one of the biggest fixed costs in AI startups. If that comes down, the barrier to entry drops another notch.

Second: AI-native enterprise cultivation. Accelerating the cultivation of "intelligence-native" enterprises — companies born from day one with deep AI dependency, not traditional businesses with an AI layer on top. This means policy resources will tilt toward truly AI-native startups, rather than being spread thinly everywhere.

Third: supporting policy exploration. Exploring the implementation of supporting policies like residency/housing and medical insurance based on enterprises' self-evaluation results. The subtext here: in the future, even a one-person company might get access to the same public services and benefits that big-company employees enjoy. That's the most tangible sense of security for founders.

Of course, policy is just an external condition. Whether a startup succeeds ultimately depends on product, market, and execution. But there's no denying it: when AI pushes the marginal cost of starting a business toward zero, and when policy gives one-person companies official recognition, more people will be willing to try.

Over the next three years, we might see an AI startup wave unlike anything before — not the VC-funded, burn-money kind, but a wave of solo founders starting from a small niche with one computer and a stack of AI tools, growing steadily. They might never become unicorns. But they'll be the most vibrant part of the economic ecosystem.

See you tomorrow.

briefs.body_html:
Midjourney的用户最近大概都在做同一件事：把自己之前生成的那些静图，变成会动的短视频。

8月初还只有Pro和Mega订阅者能用上的HD视频功能，不到一个月就全面开放给了Standard套餐用户。720p分辨率、图生视频、可选文本提示引导动效——曾经要额外付费的高级功能，现在基础套餐就能用。

速度快得不像Midjourney的作风。以前一个v6版本能磨半年，现在视频功能从内测到全档位开放只用了几个月。

从静到动，为什么是现在

Midjourney做视频，不是什么意外。作为全球最大的AI图像生成平台之一，它天然拥有向视频延伸的用户基础和技术积累。但为什么是2026年下半年这个时间点全面铺开？

答案是竞争。

视频生成赛道现在热闹得很：Runway已经迭代到了Gen 4.5，Pika的动画风格独树一帜，可灵3.0在中文社区快速起量，Sora虽然还是邀请制但标杆效应明显。每一家都在抢用户、抢场景、抢创作者心智。

Midjourney最大的优势是存量用户和内容生态。全球有数百万创作者已经在用Midjourney做图了——他们的工作流、审美、素材库，全都建立在这个平台上。现在平台说「你之前做的图，可以一键变成视频」，这些用户没有理由不试。迁移成本为零，体验却是全新的。

目前Midjourney的视频功能还比较基础：5秒时长、基于单张图片生成动效、支持文本提示引导运动方向和风格。跟Sora那种能讲完整故事的长视频比，还有不小距离。但别忘了，Midjourney的用户最擅长的是什么？用有限的工具做出惊艳的作品。给他们一个5秒的视频生成器，他们能玩出多少花来，没人知道。

创意工具的全链路时代

Midjourney做视频这件事，背后有一个更大的趋势：AI创意工具正在从「单品」走向「全链路」。

前两年，每个工具只做一件事——有的做图、有的做视频、有的做音乐、有的做文案。创作者要在好几个平台之间来回切换，流程碎、成本高、体验割裂。

现在不一样了。头部玩家都在横向扩张：Midjourney从图到视频、Runway从视频到图像编辑、Canva从设计到文案到视频全链路覆盖、字节的可灵也在图文视频音乐之间打通。用户不需要那么多工具了，一个平台能搞定大部分事情，为什么还要到处跑？

这对中小创意工具来说不是个好消息。当巨头开始做全链路，单点工具的生存空间会被挤压。要么被收购、要么做垂类深耕、要么被边缘化。但对创作者来说是好事——工具越少、效率越高、创意的注意力成本越低。

Midjourney的视频才刚刚起步，5秒的时长、720p的分辨率，跟专业视频工具比还有差距。但有一件事是确定的：最懂审美、最懂创作者的那个团队，正式入局视频了。

接下来的半年，视频生成的质量和可用性会再上一个台阶。对创作者来说，这是最好的时代——工具越来越强、越来越便宜、越来越顺手。剩下的唯一问题是：你的创意，跟上了吗？

明天见。
briefs.body_html_en:
Midjourney users have all been doing the same thing lately: taking all those still images they generated before and turning them into moving short clips.

The HD video feature — only available to Pro and Mega subscribers at the beginning of August — opened up fully to Standard plan users in less than a month. 720p resolution, image-to-video, optional text prompts to guide motion — what used to be a premium feature is now available on the basic tier.

It's moving faster than Midjourney's usual pace. The v6 image model took half a year of polishing. Video went from beta to all-tier availability in just a few months.

From Still to Motion — Why Now?

Midjourney getting into video isn't a surprise. As one of the world's largest AI image generation platforms, it naturally has the user base and technical积累 to extend into video. But why roll it out broadly in the second half of 2026?

The answer is competition.

The video generation space is heating up fast: Runway is already on Gen 4.5, Pika dominates the animation niche, Kling 3.0 is growing rapidly in Chinese-speaking markets, and Sora — while still invite-only — has set the quality bar. Everyone is fighting for users, for use cases, for creator mindshare.

Midjourney's biggest advantage is its existing user base and content ecosystem. Millions of creators worldwide already use Midjourney for imagery — their workflows, aesthetics, asset libraries, all built on this platform. Now the platform says "that image you made? Turn it into video with one click." There's zero reason for these users not to try. Zero migration cost, brand new experience.

Right now, Midjourney's video feature is still relatively basic: 5-second clips, motion generated from a single image, text prompts to guide direction and style. Compared to Sora's story-driven long-form video, there's still a big gap. But let's not forget what Midjourney users are best at: making stunning work with limited tools. Give them a 5-second video generator, and nobody knows how creative they'll get.

The End-to-End Era of Creative Tools

Midjourney moving into video fits a bigger trend: AI creative tools are evolving from "single-purpose products" to "full-stack platforms."

A couple of years ago, each tool did one thing — some did images, some did video, some did music, some did copywriting. Creators jumped between platforms, workflows were fragmented, costs added up, the experience was disjointed.

Not anymore. The top players are all expanding horizontally: Midjourney from images to video, Runway from video to image editing, Canva covering design to copy to video end-to-end, ByteDance's Kling connecting images, text, video, and audio. Users don't need so many tools anymore. When one platform handles most things, why bother switching around?

That's not great news for smaller creative tools. When giants go end-to-end, single-point tools get squeezed. Either you get acquired, you go deep into a niche, or you get marginalized. But for creators, it's a good thing — fewer tools, higher efficiency, lower cognitive overhead for creativity.

Midjourney's video journey is just getting started. 5-second clips at 720p — there's still a gap compared to professional video tools. But one thing is certain: the team that best understands aesthetics and creators has officially entered the video game.

Over the next six months, video generation quality and usability will jump another level. For creators, this is the best of times — tools are getting more powerful, cheaper, and easier to use. The only question left is: is your creativity keeping up?

See you tomorrow.

briefs.body_html:
两个机器人在台上你一拳我一拳，出拳、格挡、躲闪、连续攻防转换——没有遥控器、没有预设脚本、没有工作人员在后面拉线。全程由世界模型实时驱动。

9月7日晚间，宇树科技放出了这段视频，9月8日全网刷屏。演示基于宇树自研的UnifoLM-X2-1.0世界-动作大模型完成，号称全球首次实现由世界模型实时驱动的全自主人形机器人格斗。

很多人第一反应是：机器人打架？有啥用？搞个噱头而已。

恰恰相反。格斗可能是人形机器人最有价值的benchmark之一。

为什么格斗是终极benchmark

要理解这件事的分量，你得先明白：机器人最不怕的是结构化场景，最怕的是高动态、强交互、不可预测的场景。

工厂里的机械臂，重复同一个动作几千万次，精度可以做到丝米级——那是因为环境是固定的、任务是确定的、不需要临场决策。但真实世界是什么样的？是动态的、是变化的、是你永远不知道下一秒会发生什么的。

格斗场景把这种不确定性推到了极致。想象一下机器人要做什么：

· 实时感知：毫秒级识别对手的动作、姿势、速度、方向
· 瞬时决策：判断是出拳还是格挡、是进攻还是撤退、打哪个部位
· 精准控制：决策后毫秒级调动全身关节执行，不能慢半拍
· 动态平衡：出拳时不能自己先摔了，被推一下要能站稳
· 攻防转换：上一秒还在进攻，下一秒要立刻防守，反应时间零点几秒

这一套链路下来，感知延迟、计算效率、控制精度，每一项都被推到极限。任何一个环节掉链子，场面立刻就垮了。

所以格斗不是目的，格斗是检验感知-决策-控制全链路实时性的终极压力测试。能在格斗场景里稳住的机器人，放到搬运、巡检、家政这些低动态场景里，才是降维打击。

世界模型+动作模型的闭环

这次宇树演示的核心，是它的世界模型和动作模型做成了一个闭环。

之前的很多机器人演示，其实是「感知+规划」分开做的——摄像头看到了什么，然后大模型慢慢规划，规划完了再发给控制器执行。延迟是秒级的。走路、端水这种慢动作还能对付，打拳肯定不行。

UnifoLM-X2的突破在于：把世界模型的推演能力和动作模型的执行能力打通了，实现了瞬时规划、决策和动态交互执行。机器人不是看到动作再慢慢想怎么应对，而是用世界模型预测对手的下一步，提前做出反应。

宇树CEO王兴兴之前说过一句话很实在：机器人的最终目标还是能真正干活，要在80%的陌生场景中完成80%的任务，理想状态也要2-3年。这话放在一堆hype的机器人行业里，显得格外清醒。

人形机器人行业现在最大的问题是什么？是Demo好看，落地难。展台上能走两步、能端个杯子，一到真实场景就各种掉链子。宇树用格斗这种「极端场景」做测试，反而是一种更务实的做法——先在最难的场景里把链路打通，再往下做简单场景就容易了。

从运动控制到世界模型，从单机演示到自主对抗，具身智能的进步速度比很多人预想的要快。机器人打架当然没有商业价值，但它背后的技术，会用在你未来每天接触的每一台机器人身上。

明天见。
briefs.body_html_en:
Two robots on a stage, trading punches — jab, block, dodge, continuous offense-defense transitions. No remote controls, no pre-scripted moves, no staff pulling strings. The whole thing is driven in real time by a world model.

On the evening of September 7, Unitree released the video, and it went viral across the Chinese web on September 8. The demo runs on Unitree's in-house UnifoLM-X2-1.0 world-action foundation model, billed as the world's first fully autonomous humanoid robot combat driven in real time by a world model.

A lot of people's first reaction: robots fighting? What's the point? Just a gimmick.

Quite the opposite. Combat might be one of the most valuable benchmarks for humanoid robots.

Why Combat Is the Ultimate Benchmark

To grasp the significance here, you first need to understand: robots are least afraid of structured scenarios. What terrifies them is high-dynamics, high-interaction, unpredictable environments.

A factory robotic arm can repeat the same motion tens of millions of times with micrometer precision — because the environment is fixed, the task is deterministic, and no on-the-spot decision-making is needed. But what's the real world like? It's dynamic, it changes, you never know what's coming next.

Combat pushes that uncertainty to the extreme. Think about what a robot has to do:

· Real-time perception: millisecond-level recognition of the opponent's movements, posture, speed, direction
· Instant decision-making: judge whether to punch or block, attack or retreat, target where
· Precise control: after deciding, activate full-body joints in milliseconds — can't be a beat slow
· Dynamic balance: can't fall over mid-punch, has to stay stable when pushed
· Offense-defense transitions: one second attacking, next second defending — reaction time in the hundreds of milliseconds

Running through this whole pipeline pushes perception latency, compute efficiency, and control precision all to their limits. If any link in the chain fails, the whole thing falls apart immediately.

So combat isn't the goal. Combat is the ultimate stress test for the real-time perception-decision-control pipeline. A robot that can hold its own in a fight will dominate lower-dynamic scenarios like carrying, inspection, and household tasks — that's a trickle-down effect.

The Closed Loop of World Model + Action Model

The core of Unitree's demo is that its world model and action model form a closed loop.

In many previous robot demos, perception and planning were done separately — the camera sees something, the LLM slowly plans it out, then sends the plan to the controller for execution. Latency is measured in seconds. Fine for walking slowly or carrying water, but totally inadequate for fighting.

UnifoLM-X2's breakthrough is connecting the world model's predictive capability with the action model's execution capability, achieving instant planning, decision-making, and dynamic interactive execution. The robot doesn't see an action and then slowly figure out how to respond — it uses the world model to predict the opponent's next move and react ahead of time.

Unitree CEO Wang Xingxing said something very grounded earlier: the ultimate goal of robots is still actually getting work done. To complete 80% of tasks in 80% of unfamiliar scenes will take ideally 2–3 years. In an industry full of hype, that kind of sobriety stands out.

The biggest problem in the humanoid robot industry right now is this: demos look great, but real-world deployment is hard. They can walk a few steps on stage, hold a cup — but throw them into a real scenario and everything breaks. Unitree using an "extreme scenario" like combat for testing is actually a more pragmatic approach — get the pipeline working in the hardest scenario first, then working downward to simpler scenarios becomes easy.

From motion control to world models, from single-unit demos to autonomous对抗, embodied AI is advancing faster than many people expected. Robot fighting obviously has no commercial value. But the technology behind it will find its way into every robot you interact with in the future.

See you tomorrow.

briefs.body_html:
一条叫《早餐奶奶》的AI短视频，在抖音上拿了2.5亿播放、1509万点赞。

你猜它的创作者是什么背景？专业导演？MCN机构？大厂设计师？都不是。答案是：一个之前没做过短视频的普通人，用AI工具一个人做出来的。

这不是孤例。2026年上半年，抖音的AI内容生态正在经历一场爆发——涌现出9条破亿视频、20个半年涨粉超50万的账号。参与「OiiOii创作者计划」的0基础创作者们，只用了1个多月，累计播放量就达到了12亿。

注意，是累计12亿，不是单人。但即便如此，这个数字也足够惊人——它意味着AI内容创作的门槛，已经低到了一个前所未有的程度。

一人军团模式的规模化

传统短视频的生产模式是什么样的？一个团队——编剧、拍摄、剪辑、运营，少则三五人，多则十几人。产能有限，成本不低，能不能出爆款还要看运气。

AI时代的模式是：一个人，就是一支军团。

AI工具已经能覆盖短视频生产的几乎所有环节：文案生成、脚本拆分、画面生成、数字人口播、配音配乐、字幕、封面、标题、标签……以前需要好几个岗位配合的工作流，现在一个人加上AI工具就能搞定。

更可怕的是迭代速度。传统团队做一条视频，从选题到发布可能要三五天。AI创作者呢？一天产出十几条不是什么难事。数量级的差异，直接改变了内容生产的游戏规则——以前是精雕细琢碰运气，现在是快速试错、数据驱动、批量生产。

当然，量多不代表质高。9条破亿的背后，可能是几百条几千播放的炮灰。但这恰恰是AI内容生产的优势：试错成本几乎为零。一条没爆？没关系，下一条。十条没爆？第二十条可能就爆了。传统团队试错十次的成本，AI创作者可以试错一百次。

内容产业的供给侧革命

这件事最大的影响，不是多了几亿播放，也不是多了几个网红账号。而是内容产业的供给侧，被彻底改写了。

以前内容行业最大的瓶颈是什么？是人。好的创作者是稀缺资源，培养一个成熟的内容创作者需要好几年。MCN机构的核心竞争力，就是签下最多的好创作者。

AI把这个瓶颈打破了。0基础的人，经过简单培训就能上手做内容，而且产能还不低。这意味着内容供给会出现爆炸式增长——以后不缺内容了，缺的是注意力。

供给爆炸之后，会发生什么？

首先是平均质量先降后升。一开始大量低质量AI内容涌入，平台上充斥着同质化的东西。但很快，用户审美疲劳了，纯粹靠数量堆的打法会失效。能活下来的，还是那些有独特审美、有个人风格、有真实表达的创作者——AI只是他们的放大器。

其次是内容的个性化程度会大幅提高。当生产内容的成本趋近于零，给每个人定制专属内容就变得可行了。以后你刷到的每条视频，可能都是专门为你生成的。

最后是传统MCN模式会受到冲击。一个人就能干一个团队的活，为什么还要签MCN分成？当然MCN也有资源和经验的优势，但它们必须转型——从经纪人模式转向服务模式，给AI创作者提供工具、培训、商业化对接。

12亿播放只是一个开始。AI内容创作的浪潮才刚刚起来，接下来的一两年，我们会看到更多让人惊掉下巴的数据和案例。

但有一件事是不变的：工具再强，最后拼的还是创意和审美。AI可以降低门槛、提高效率，但它不能替你想出来要表达什么。真正好的内容，永远是人脑里出来的东西。

明天见。
briefs.body_html_en:
An AI short video called "Breakfast Grandma" got 250 million views and 15.09 million likes on Douyin.

Guess what the creator's background is? A professional director? An MCN agency? A designer from a big tech company? None of the above. The answer: an ordinary person who'd never made short videos before, made it by themselves with AI tools.

This isn't an isolated case. In the first half of 2026, Douyin's AI content ecosystem is going through an explosion — 9 videos breaking 100 million views, 20 accounts gaining over 500,000 followers in half a year. Zero-experience creators participating in the "OiiOii Creator Program" hit a cumulative 1.2 billion views in just over a month.

Note: that's 1.2 billion cumulative, not per person. But even so, the number is staggering — it means the barrier to AI content creation has dropped to an unprecedented level.

The One-Person Army Model Goes Scale

What's the traditional short video production model? A team — screenwriter, filming, editing, operations — three to five people at minimum, sometimes over a dozen. Limited output, high costs, and whether you get a hit still depends on luck.

The AI era model is: one person, one army.

AI tools already cover almost every环节 of short video production: copy generation, script breakdown, image generation, digital human presenters, voiceover and music, subtitles, thumbnails, titles, tags… a workflow that used to require several different roles can now be handled by one person with AI tools.

What's even more striking is the iteration speed. A traditional team might take three to five days from concept to publish for one video. AI creators? Cranking out a dozen a day is nothing. An order-of-magnitude difference in quantity directly changes the rules of the content game — before, you refined and polished and hoped for luck; now, it's fast testing, data-driven, batch production.

Of course, more volume doesn't mean higher quality. Behind those 9 viral 100M-view videos, there might be hundreds of flops with a few thousand views each. But that's exactly the advantage of AI content production: the cost of failure is nearly zero. One didn't go viral? No problem — next one. Ten didn't work? The twentieth might.

The Supply-Side Revolution of the Content Industry

The biggest impact here isn't a few billion more views, or a handful of new influencer accounts. It's that the supply side of the content industry has been completely rewritten.

What used to be the biggest bottleneck in the content industry? People. Good creators are a scarce resource. Cultivating a mature content creator takes years. An MCN's core competitive advantage is signing the most good creators.

AI breaks that bottleneck. People with zero experience, after simple training, can get started making content — and their output isn't low. This means content supply will explode — soon there won't be a shortage of content; there'll be a shortage of attention.

After supply explodes, what happens?

First, average quality drops then rises. At first, a flood of low-quality AI content pours in, platforms are full of homogeneous stuff. But soon, users grow tired of it, and the pure-volume approach stops working. What survives are creators with unique aesthetics, personal style, authentic expression — AI is just their amplifier.

Second, content personalization will increase dramatically. When the cost of producing content approaches zero, customizing exclusive content for each person becomes feasible. In the future, every video you scroll past might be generated specifically for you.

Third, the traditional MCN model will be disrupted. If one person can do the work of a team, why sign with an MCN and give up a cut? MCNs of course have resources and experience advantages, but they'll have to transform — from talent agency model to service model, providing tools, training, and monetization support for AI creators.

1.2 billion views is just the beginning. The wave of AI content creation is just getting started. Over the next year or two, we'll see even more jaw-dropping data and cases.

But one thing stays the same: no matter how powerful the tools, the final competition is still creativity and taste. AI can lower barriers and boost efficiency, but it can't think of what to express for you. Truly good content always comes from the human mind.

See you tomorrow.

cao.body_html:
朋友们，今天这个槽点，说出来你可能不信：AI领域最成功的落地应用，可能是帮骗子提高了诈骗效率。

广州最近查处了一起AI培训诈骗案，三家关联公司被查，累计投诉超过200件，同一个法定代表人因涉嫌诈骗被依法逮捕。

套路有多老套？跟十年前的Java培训班、五年前的电商运营课、两年前的短视频变现课，简直一模一样——只不过把关键词换成了「AI」。

「躺赚」是怎么变成「躺枪」的

让我们来复盘一下这套成熟的流水线作业，你品你细品。

第一步，免费课引流。在抖音、小红书、视频号上疯狂投放广告，标题永远是「零基础学AI，月入过万」「AI时代再不学就晚了」「35岁转行AI的最佳路径」。点进去是9.9元甚至0元的体验课，先把你拉进群再说。

第二步，制造焦虑+画饼。课上讲什么？讲AI有多火、讲别人靠AI赚了多少钱、讲你再不学就要被时代淘汰了。放几张不知道哪来的「学员收益截图」，讲几个「宝妈靠AI月入三万」的励志故事。你听得热血沸腾，觉得自己也行了。

第三步，高价班收割。体验课快结束了，老师开始推「高阶班」「私教课」「就业直通车」，价格从几千到几万不等。注意了，这时候他们不会催你交钱——他们会贴心地说「没钱没关系，可以分期」，然后给你推荐各种网贷平台。

第四步，交钱即失联。等你真交了钱，要么课程内容跟体验课完全不是一回事，全是网上就能搜到的二手资料；要么所谓的「内推就业」根本就是敷衍；更狠的直接跑路，群解散、老师消失、客服不回。你想退费？合同里早埋好了「开课不退费」「违约金30%」的坑。

一整套流程下来，从「我要学AI改变命运」到「我怎么欠了几万贷款」，可能只需要一两个星期。

骗子永远冲在最前面

说起来也挺讽刺的。每次有什么新风口，第一个冲进去的永远是骗子。

区块链火的时候，骗子卖矿机、搞传销币、做资金盘，比真正做技术的还积极。元宇宙火的时候，骗子卖虚拟地产、搞元宇宙投资、开元宇宙培训班。AI火了，骗子又第一时间换上了AI的马甲——AI培训、AI带货、AI数字人、AI理财、AI相亲……只有你想不到的，没有骗子不能蹭的。

而且他们比正经创业者勤奋多了：投放力度更大、话术迭代更快、转化率算得更精、团队执行力更强。创业公司可能还在打磨产品，骗子已经跑通了从获客到收割的全链路SOP。

更气人的是什么？是他们透支了整个行业的信任。本来想正经学AI的人，踩过一次坑之后，对所有AI课程都心存戒备。真正在做AI教育的团队，反而被这些老鼠屎连累了。

好了，吐槽归吐槽，给大家几条实用提醒，都是血泪教训堆出来的：

第一，凡是承诺「包就业」「躺赚」「月入过万」的，一律拉黑。真有这么赚钱的路子，他自己不去赚，来教你？用脚趾头想都知道有问题。

第二，凡是让你办网贷、分期付学费的，扭头就走。学习是投资，但加杠杆学习不是投资，是赌博，而且你大概率会输。

第三，学AI最好的方法永远是动手做，不是报班。免费教程、开源项目、社区讨论，这些资源多到用不完。真想学，从一个具体的小项目开始，边做边学，比花几万块上课有用多了。

AI是个好东西，但风口越大，猪和骗子就越多。保持清醒，别让「改变命运」的期待，变成「欠了一屁股债」的现实。

今天就槽到这里，明天继续。
cao.body_html_en:
Folks, today's hot take might be hard to believe: the most successfully deployed application of AI might be how it's helped scammers improve their fraud efficiency.

Guangzhou recently busted an AI training scam ring. Three affiliated companies were investigated, cumulative complaints exceeded 200, and the same legal representative was arrested on suspicion of fraud.

How original is the套路? It's identical to the Java bootcamps from ten years ago, the e-commerce operations courses from five years ago, the short-video monetization classes from two years ago — they just swapped the keyword to "AI."

How "Easy Money" Turns Into "Got Scammed"

Let's walk through this well-oiled assembly line. Take a sip of tea and savor the details.

Step one: free classes as bait. They flood Douyin, Xiaohongshu, and video platforms with ads. Headlines are always the same — "Learn AI from zero, make 10K a month," "It's too late if you don't learn AI now," "The best path for 35-year-olds to switch careers to AI." Click through and it's a ¥9.9 or even free trial class. First, just get you into the group chat.

Step two: manufacture anxiety + paint a picture of wealth. What do they teach in class? How hot AI is, how much money other people are making with AI, how you'll be left behind by the times if you don't learn now. Throw in a few "student earnings screenshots" from who knows where, tell a few inspirational stories about "stay-at-home moms making 30K a month with AI." You leave feeling fired up, thinking you can do it too.

Step three: premium classes harvest you. As the trial class is ending, the instructor starts pushing "advanced courses," "private coaching," "job placement express" — prices ranging from a few thousand to tens of thousands. And here's the thing: they don't even pressure you to pay. They thoughtfully say "no money? No problem — pay in installments," then recommend various online lending platforms.

Step four: pay up, then disappear. Once you actually pay, either the course content is nothing like the trial — all second-hand material you can find online for free — or the so-called "job placement" is just lip service. The bolder ones just vanish entirely. Groups get disbanded, instructors disappear, customer support stops replying. Want a refund? The contract was already buried with clauses like "no refunds after class starts" and "30% penalty fee."

After the whole pipeline, going from "I'm gonna learn AI and change my life" to "wait, why do I owe tens of thousands in loans?" can take as little as a week or two.

Scammers Are Always First to the Party

It's kind of ironic, honestly. Every time there's a new trend, scammers are the first ones charging in.

When blockchain was hot, scammers sold mining rigs, ran pyramid schemes with crypto coins, operated investment frauds — more active than actual tech builders. When the metaverse was trending, scammers sold virtual real estate, ran metaverse investment scams, opened metaverse bootcamps. Now AI is hot, and scammers have instantly put on their AI vests — AI training, AI e-commerce, AI digital humans, AI finance, AI dating… if you can name it, a scammer has already monetized it.

And they work harder than legitimate founders. Bigger ad budgets, faster iteration on sales scripts, sharper conversion calculations, stronger team execution. While real startups are still polishing their products, scammers have already perfected the full SOP from customer acquisition to harvest.

What's even more infuriating? They erode trust in the entire industry. People who genuinely wanted to learn AI, after getting burned once, become suspicious of all AI courses. Teams that are actually doing AI education end up collateral damage from these bad apples.

Alright, venting aside — here are some practical tips, forged from real血泪教训:

One: Anyone promising "guaranteed job," "easy money," or "10K+ per month" — block them immediately. If it were that profitable, would they be teaching you instead of doing it themselves? Think with your toes.

Two: Anyone telling you to take out loans or pay tuition in installments — walk away. Learning is an investment, but leveraged learning isn't investment — it's gambling, and you'll probably lose.

Three: The best way to learn AI is always by building, not by taking classes. Free tutorials, open-source projects, community discussions — there are more resources than you could ever use. If you really want to learn, start with a specific small project, learn by doing. Way more useful than dropping tens of thousands on a course.

AI is great. But the bigger the hype, the more pigs and scammers come along. Stay sharp. Don't let the expectation of "changing your destiny" turn into the reality of "saddled with debt."

That's all for today's rant — more tomorrow.
